---
title: "The interactive 2D/3D laboratory"
---

The laboratory is a standalone web application: all of the numerics (nLPT
recursion, sheet rasterization, Hopf–Cole solver, power spectra, loop
integrals) run in your browser in WebAssembly compiled from the Rust crate
[`core/`](https://github.com/yipihey/hopf-cole-cosmology/tree/main/core),
and the fields are rendered with WebGPU (with a Canvas2D fallback).

<p><a class="btn btn-primary btn-lg" href="../app/index.html">Open the laboratory in a new page</a></p>

```{=html}
<iframe src="../app/index.html?embed=1" style="width:100%;height:900px;border:1px solid #8884;border-radius:6px;" title="Hopf–Cole cosmology lab"></iframe>
```

## Requirements and lite mode

Everything runs in the browser; nothing is sent to a server. On a desktop
GPU use the defaults. On a laptop with an integrated GPU (or with WebGPU
disabled) the lab detects this and starts in **lite mode**: 2D at $128^2$,
CPU rendering of the sheet density, GPU compute off, 3D limited to $64^3$.
You can force it with the *Performance* control or by opening
`app/index.html?lite=1`; `?nogpu=1` disables WebGPU altogether. If the lab
ever stalls on a GPU, a banner offers both options, and the *Diagnostics*
box at the bottom of the controls lists the adapter, its limits and the
last error so that you can report them.

## Two modes

**2D (fast).** Grids from $128^2$ to $512^2$, interactive at the frame rate
of the sheet renderer. The 2D universe is the $z$-symmetric 3D universe of
[Chapter 6](06-lpt.qmd), so all coefficients are the physical ones. Use it
to build intuition: drag $D$, change the smoothing scale, switch orders and
compare with Hopf–Cole.

**3D (quantitative).** Grids from $32^3$ to $128^3$ with the full 4LPT
recursion ($\mu_3$ terms and all three curl components), tetrahedral sheet
or cloud-in-cell densities (the latter with window deconvolution), slices and
a volume rendering. Here the measured power spectra have enough modes per bin
to compare with the one-loop predictions quantitatively. With WebGPU the
per-time-step pipeline (positions, deposit, Hopf–Cole, FFTs) runs in compute
shaders, so even $128^3$ follows the $D$ slider.

## Controls

Every line plot in the laboratory (and every plot widget in the chapters)
is interactive: the mouse wheel zooms around the cursor (over the $x$ or
$y$ axis strip it zooms that axis only), dragging pans, a double click
resets, and the small toolbar under each plot switches either axis between
linear and logarithmic scaling and accepts typed axis ranges. A zoomed view
persists while the data change, so one can watch a feature at fixed axes
while dragging $D$.

| Group | Control | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Initial conditions | shape | power law $k^n$, BBKS or Eisenstein–Hu CDM-like shape; two plane waves; a single peak |
| | smoothing $R$ | Gaussian filter $e^{-k^2R^2/2}$ on $\delta_0$ (box units) |
| | $\sigma_0$ | rms of the smoothed $\delta_0$; with $\sigma_0 = 1$ the growth factor $D$ equals the rms linear density contrast |
| | seed | random phases |
| Cosmology | $\Omega_m$ | flat $\Lambda$CDM; $\Omega_m = 1$ is Einstein–de Sitter with exact $D^n$ growth, otherwise all 13 growth functions through 4LPT are integrated numerically; $a(D)$ and $\Omega_m(a)$ are displayed |
| Dynamics | $D$ | growth factor used as time; $D_{\rm sc}$ (first shell crossing of the chosen order) is displayed |
| | LPT order | 1 (Zel'dovich) to 4 |
| | $\nu$ | adhesion viscosity for the Hopf–Cole solver, in box units$^2$ |
| | Hopf–Cole method | Fourier multiplier (shows the dynamic-range failure) or log-domain kernel with 1–4× refinement |
| Views | field | sheet density (triangles in 2D, tetrahedra in 3D), CIC density, Hopf–Cole density, linear density, velocity potential, $\ln\psi$, Jacobian, LPT sources |
| | GPU compute (3D) | runs positions, CIC deposit, Hopf–Cole and the FFTs on the GPU (WebGPU compute shaders) so that $128^3$ responds live to the $D$ slider |
| | Fourier | $\log|\hat\delta(\mathbf k)|$ and phase maps of the selected field, $\log|\hat\psi(\mathbf k)|$, and the phase-only reconstruction (unit amplitudes, original phases), which peaks on the skeleton of the web |
| Legendre lab | source potential | Hopf–Cole run on the Zel'dovich potential, on the $n$LPT longitudinal potential (Legendre transform of the $n$LPT map, @sec-legendre), or with the first-order transverse correction; difference maps and spectral ratios against the sheet |
| PDFs | diameter | one-point distributions of $\log_{10}(1+\delta)$ for every method at the grid scale and in top-hat spheres (discs) of the chosen diameter in cells, with Gaussian and lognormal references and moments |
| Kernels | sweep | two-plane-wave kernel check: harmonic amplitudes at $\mathbf k_1$, $\mathbf k_1\pm\mathbf k_2$, $2\mathbf k_{1,2}$ measured from the Hopf–Cole density and the sheet, divided by $D^2$ and the initial amplitudes, against the viscous, Zel'dovich and gravitational $F_2$ (@sec-viscous-kernels); sweep over $D$ or $\nu$ |
| Statistics | $P(k)$ | measured for sheet / CIC / Hopf–Cole / linear, with 1-loop SPT and ZA predictions |
| | $r(k)$ | cross-correlation with the linear field |
| | phase sums | distribution of $\varphi(\mathbf k_1)+\varphi(\mathbf k_2)-\varphi(\mathbf k_1+\mathbf k_2)$ over closed triangles with $|\mathbf k| \le k_{\max}$ for the selected fields, unweighted or weighted by the amplitudes (bispectrum phase), with $\langle\cos\theta\rangle$ |
| | EFT fit | $c_s^2$ from $P_{\rm sheet} - P_{\rm 1\text{-}loop}$ for $k < k_{\max}$ |

## Suggested experiments

1. **Zel'dovich equals Hopf–Cole.** Order 1, small $\nu$ with the log-domain
   method, $D < D_{\rm sc}$: the sheet and Hopf–Cole density panels agree to
   the rasterization noise, and their power spectra coincide.
2. **Shell crossing.** Push $D$ past $D_{\rm sc}$. The sheet folds (wireframe
   view) and the density develops three-stream regions; the Hopf–Cole
   solution instead forms thin shocks whose thickness scales with
   $\sqrt{\nu D}$.
3. **Higher orders.** Order 2 versus 1 at fixed $D$: filaments sharpen,
   voids empty. Orders 3 and 4 change little before shell crossing; the
   order-4 source map shows where the series is working hardest.
4. **Mode coupling.** Two plane waves; watch the harmonics in the amplitude
   map; make them parallel. Open the *Kernels* section: the measured
   second-order kernel of the Hopf–Cole density follows the viscous
   $F_2^\nu$ (Zel'dovich as $\nu\to0$), the 2LPT sheet the gravitational
   $F_2$ with its tidal term; sweep $\nu$ to see the damping $e^{-\nu k^2 D}$
   that the EFT would call $c_s^2 = \nu D$.
5. **The loop and the cutoff.** Gaussian field, order 4, $D \sim 0.3$. The
   measured $P(k)$ departs from linear theory at high $k$; the 1-loop curve
   follows it up to some $k$; the EFT counterterm extends the agreement.
   Now change $R$: the loop prediction and the fitted $c_s^2$ move together.
6. **Legendre.** Open the Legendre lab, order 2, $D < D_{\rm sc}$: the
   $n$LPT-potential density differs from the sheet only by the rasterization
   noise (shrinking with $N$), while the Zel'dovich Hopf–Cole density differs by
   the genuine 2LPT correction. At order 3 read off $\Psi_T/\Psi_L$.
7. **Phases.** Compare the phase maps of the linear and evolved fields and
   the $r(k)$ curve at several $D$, for 4LPT and for Hopf–Cole at two values
   of $\nu$. Add the phase-only reconstruction panel and the phase-sum plot:
   the reconstruction traces the walls and nodes, and $\langle\cos\theta\rangle$
   grows from zero as the web forms.
